attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Create one high-resolution portrait-card fusion using exactly two inputs: Image1 is the exact original small card, serving as the sole visual authority for pose, clothing, hair, expression, light, and crop; Image2 provides only the user mascot identity and anatomy. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body with green-ringed black eyes, while strictly preserving the source-matching mouth expression. The source observation dictates a slight closed-mouth smile, so the mouth must remain closed with no broad grin or invented tooth row. Retain the actual short grey-brown wavy hair swept up and back from a receding hairline, the visible eyebrow hair, and the clearly defined dark upper-lip moustache with mildly curved ends and a smooth chin. Do not add caps, spectacles, or beards. Maintain the dark grey charcoal open-lapel suit, white pale shirt, and distinct red burgundy tie visible beside the note. The geometry must feature a distinct rounded chin immediately meeting a raised and broadened original neckline with minimal throat exposure, creating a very short broad neck transition without any separate yellow shaft, pointed V-shaped yellow funnel, narrow human collar, neck rolls, floating collar, clipping, or cream belly bib. Keep the actual garment open style and fastening coherent, with front collar fabric overlapping the short base and rear fabric behind it, showing proper seam and contact shadows. Include the complete tilted dark frame, opaque grey photo backing, and the overlapping lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper strokes retained exactly as cropped and occluded. All original solid surfaces must remain opaque, with genuine transparency only outside the complete card silhouette. Avoid extra figures, hidden decorations, readable writing, labels, watermarks, comparison boards, or new backdrops. Do not infer from names or biographies; keep fine details genuinely indistinct understated.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: Bareheaded nearly frontal bust with original mild head angle and slight CLOSED-MOUTH smile, no broad grin or invented tooth row. Short GREY-BROWN wavy hair swept up/back from a receding hairline, actual eyebrow HAIR and a clearly visible dark UPPER-LIP MOUSTACHE with mildly curved ends, smooth chin. Dark grey/charcoal OPEN-lapel suit, white/pale shirt and distinct RED/BURGUNDY tie visible beside the note. Preserve this exact hair volume and red tie variant, no cap, spectacles or beard.
Keep the exact source head angle and mouth expression. The whole visible yellow area above the raised/broadened collar is one compact near-round head with a rounded chin: no additional separate yellow neck segment, pointed V or shaft below it. Keep actual garment fastening and source open/closed collar state; no extra accessories or readable writing. Mascot reference supplies identity only and cannot erase source hair.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
